calls.beyond: Los Angeles is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 5.8% against Los Angeles) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Solberg scores his first two NHL goals, but the Ducks lose
paras: Stian Solberg, in his fifth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Mikael Granlund, midway through the first to open the scoring for the Ducks. He scored his second NHL goal a little over a minute later to make it 2-0. It was a busy second period. Mats Zuccarello scored twice and Adrian Kempe once in less than eight minutes in the first half of the second to turn a 2-0 deficit into a 3-2 lead. Beckett Sennecke tied it up for Anaheim on the power play less than four minutes later, but that was the last goal the Ducks would get. Andre Lee put the Kings ahead for good early in the third, and Trevor Moore sealed it into the empty net with less than two minutes left.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Darcy Kuemper made 25 saves for the Kings, and Laurent Brossoit stopped 16 of 20 at the other end. The Kings moved to 9-12-2, seventh in the Pacific, while the Ducks dropped to 12-14-1, slipping to fifth in the Pacific.
